title: Rule resolver output contract
description: Shape of the value a deterministic rule resolver returns for one work item, per standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md. This is the contract of a function's return value, not a registry file: it carries no $schema/schema_version envelope of its own, and nothing here is committed data waiting to be validated by the generic registry pass. PHASE C (implementation of the resolver) and PHASE F (population of the data this contract is computed from) are out of scope for the schema itself.

applicable_norms.description: Norms found applicable, one entry per norm. Fragments of one container norm are separate entries, never merged into one: standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §1, delivery does not determine content.

applicable_protocols.description: Protocols routed from work_kind or change_class. Several change_class values may route to one protocol; one change_class does not receive several incompatible mandatory protocols without an explicit composition named at the route record itself (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §7).

required_verification.description: References to a verification router, smoke-protocol or regression-testing path.

unresolved_applicability.description: Norms whose applicability the resolver could not decide deterministically — scope, activation, source or a conflict left open (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4) — not norms whose instruction-intake verdict merely has not been unified yet. A deferred intake verdict does not by itself put its subject here. This array is about norm applicability only; obstacles to decomposing an initiative go in unresolved_items, and the two are never merged.

unresolved_items.description: Obstacles that stop a work_kind: initiative from being decomposed into child work items — for example the source-repository list is incomplete (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §6). This is a separate, always-present array, distinct in kind from unresolved_applicability: an unresolved item is missing input for decomposition, not a norm whose applicability is undecidable. Empty for every non-initiative work item and for an initiative that has already been decomposed.

requires_reresolution.description: True when changed_paths diverged from the candidate_paths a previous resolution for the same work item used. The resolver does not extend the prior applicable_norms heuristically on that divergence; it reports the need for a fresh call.

decomposition_required.description: True when work_kind is initiative and an explicit list of child work items has not yet been supplied (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §6). False for every non-initiative work item and for an initiative already decomposed.

applicable_initiative_protocol.description: Identifier of the decomposition protocol for this initiative, if one is already declared for its kind; null when none is declared yet. Present (possibly null) regardless of work_kind, so that the output shape does not change with the input.

pre_decomposition_norms.description: Product-wide norms applicable to an initiative before it is decomposed into child work items — for example a requirement on a parity registry used to reconcile the initiative's source editions.

norm.description: Identifier of the norm — a reference to its instruction-intake record, or to its Kernel path when it never went through intake.

activation_reason.description: Which axis or mask fired, in the vocabulary of activation in registries/rule-resolution/applicability.schema.json — not a free restatement, so that the output stays checkable against the applicability record it came from.

source.description: Same three values as registries/rule-resolution/applicability.schema.json record.source for a norm. Distinct from a protocol route's source pool below — a norm and a route answer different questions.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the norm at resolution time, so the output is checkable the same way an instruction-intake record is: by recomputing the digest, not by trusting the label.

routed_from.description: The work_kind or change_class value that produced this route — one pool, because a route may be keyed on either (standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §7).

source.description: Where the routing line came from: Kernel carries universal routes, Instance/repository may add a product- or repository-specific route, and a local record never silently overrides a universal one — disagreement is a conflict entry above, not a silent replacement.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the route record at resolution time. A route record carries either this or revision, whichever its own store identifies it by; not both are required, and neither is optional in isolation — at least one is (see allOf below).

revision.description: VCS revision the route record was read at, used instead of digest when the record's home identifies it by revision rather than by content hash.

norms.description: The norms or routes in conflict — including two incompatible mandatory change_class → protocol routes, standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §7, not only conflicting agent norms.

reason.description: Which axis or claim they contradict on.

Why this norm's applicability is not deterministically decidable today — scope, activation, source or conflict left open, per standards/workspace/rule-resolution.md §4. Not used to record a subject whose intake verdict is merely deferred while its runtime applicability is otherwise decided, and not used for a decomposition obstacle, which is a decomposition_blocker in unresolved_items.

decomposition_blocker.description: One missing input that must be supplied before a work_kind: initiative can be decomposed. Deliberately shaped and named apart from unresolved: item, not subject, so the two arrays cannot be filled from one code path.

item.description: What is missing for decomposition — for example "complete list of source repositories".

reason.description: Why decomposition cannot proceed without it.
